words.meaning: Force used to influence others' decisions.

medium.simple_explanation: Using persuasion or force to influence someone's decisions.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like when your mom gives you 'The Look' until you finally agree to clean your room.

examples.text: Pressure groups try to convince the government to change certain laws.
My cat puts extreme pressure on me to share my tuna sandwich by staring into my soul.

words.meaning: Groups working for a shared social goal.

medium.simple_explanation: Groups of people working together over time to achieve a specific social or political goal.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a massive, real-life group chat where everyone actually agrees to get off the couch and change the world.

examples.text: Environmental movements work hard to protect our oceans from pollution.
The 'No Homework on Fridays' movement was sadly shut down by the principal.

words.meaning: To put forth effort or use power.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to describe how pressure groups put effort and power into the political system to get results.
hard.simple_explanation: To use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like when you use all your might to 'exert' pressure on the last bit of toothpaste in the tube to make it come out.

examples.text: Pressure groups exert influence on the government to change laws.
I had to exert all my brainpower just to remember where I hid my secret stash of cookies.

hard.real_world_analogy: A weightlifter using all their strength to lift a heavy barbell.

words.meaning: Power to affect how others act.

medium.simple_explanation: The power to change how someone thinks, acts, or makes decisions.
medium.funny_explanation: It's that magical power your best friend has to convince you that neon orange pants are actually a good idea.

examples.text: Social media can have a huge influence on what people choose to buy.
The smell of fresh pizza has a strange influence over my ability to focus on math.

words.meaning: Activities related to governing a country.

medium.simple_explanation: The activities and debates involved in running a country or a local government.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically a giant game of 'Who Gets to Hold the TV Remote,' but for the entire country.

examples.text: Many people join groups to get involved in local politics and help their town.
Deciding who gets the last slice of cake involves some very serious family politics.

words.meaning: To give details about something in words.

medium.simple_explanation: To give a detailed account or picture of something using words.
medium.funny_explanation: What you have to do when you try to tell your friends about the 'massive' spider in your room that was actually the size of a grain of rice.

examples.text: The textbook asks us to describe how a pressure group works.
It is hard to describe the taste of water, but we all know when it tastes 'crispy' at 3 AM.

words.meaning: Different types or kinds of something.
Way in which two things are connected.

medium.simple_explanation: The way in which two or more people, groups, or things are connected.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the complicated bond between a student and their alarm clock—it's mostly just loud noises and resentment.

examples.text: The relationship between voters and leaders is very important in a democracy.
My relationship with my bed is very serious; we spend at least eight hours together every night.

words.meaning: To make something clear with details.

medium.simple_explanation: To make something clear or easy to understand by providing more details.
medium.funny_explanation: What you have to do when you're caught with cookie crumbs on your face and your mom asks where the cookies went.

examples.text: Can you explain the main goal of this political party?
Try to explain to a cat why it can't sit on your laptop while you're working.

words.meaning: Things people do to achieve a goal.

medium.simple_explanation: Things that people do, especially for a particular purpose or for fun.
medium.funny_explanation: For some people, this means sports; for me, it usually means professional-level snacking.

examples.text: The group's activities included holding rallies and writing letters to the mayor.
My weekend activities mostly involve looking for my phone while I'm holding it.

words.meaning: Working or operating in a certain way.

medium.simple_explanation: Working or operating in the correct or proper way.
medium.funny_explanation: How your brain is supposed to work during a test, but usually, it just plays the 'Baby Shark' song on repeat.

examples.text: A fair election is necessary for the proper functioning of a democracy.
My brain stops functioning the moment I see a 'Pull' sign on a 'Push' door.

words.meaning: System where people vote for their leaders.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This word is used to describe a government system where power is shared and people have a say.
hard.simple_explanation: A system where everyone has a right to vote or share their opinion in decision-making.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine a household where the kids get to vote on whether dinner is broccoli or pizza—that's a democratic kitchen!

examples.text: In a democratic government, people have the right to express their views.
Our club is democratic; we even voted on whether the mascot should be a dragon or a taco.

hard.real_world_analogy: A classroom where students vote on which game to play during recess.

words.meaning: Things that show what others are like.
Way in which things are not alike.
Groups formed for a specific purpose.

medium.simple_explanation: Groups of people who join together to achieve a shared goal.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a school club, but with more serious meetings and slightly fewer juice boxes.

examples.text: Many international organisations work to provide clean water to villages.
I’m starting an organisation for people who walk into a room and immediately forget why.

words.meaning: To start a task or take responsibility.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the act of organizations starting or taking responsibility for specific tasks or projects.
hard.simple_explanation: To commit yourself to a task or begin a project.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like when you 'undertake' the mission of cleaning your room, even though you know it's going to be a long journey.

examples.text: The group decided to undertake a protest to protect the park.
I shall undertake the dangerous task of asking my brother to share his chocolate.

hard.real_world_analogy: A knight accepting a quest from a king.

words.meaning: To help something grow or succeed.

medium.simple_explanation: To support or encourage something so that it becomes more popular or successful.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you tell everyone your dog is a 'genius' just because he finally stopped chasing his own tail.

examples.text: The posters were put up to promote the school's recycling program.
I am here to promote the idea that naps should be a mandatory school subject.

words.meaning: Things that provide advantage to a group.

medium.simple_explanation: The things that a person or group cares about or wants to protect.
medium.funny_explanation: Usually, my primary interests involve chocolate and avoiding any form of cardio.

examples.text: Sectional groups focus on the interests of a specific group of workers.
It is in my best interests not to tell my sister I accidentally broke her headphones.

words.meaning: Relating clearly to one thing only.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to one particular thing rather than being general.
medium.funny_explanation: When your mom says 'Clean your room,' she means specific things, like the laundry mountain under your bed.

examples.text: The lawyer asked the witness a very specific question about the time of the event.
I have a specific talent for always finding the one shopping cart with a squeaky wheel.

words.meaning: Relating to people living in communities.
Parts or groups within a larger whole.
People who do a job for pay.
People who work for another person.

medium.simple_explanation: People who are paid to work for a company or another person.
medium.funny_explanation: Human beings who trade their free time for money so they can buy things they are too tired to use.

examples.text: The employees at the factory went on strike to ask for better pay.
If I were one of Santa's employees, I'd probably get fired for 'sampling' too many cookies.

words.meaning: People who help others to learn.
People who give legal advice and help.
Better or different from what is usual.
An important part of something.

medium.simple_explanation: A distinctive part or quality of something.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the 'silent mode' on your phone—the most important feature when you're supposed to be studying.

examples.text: One important feature of a pressure group is that they don't try to win elections.
My best physical feature is definitely my ability to wiggle my ears when I'm nervous.

words.meaning: Shows the difference between two things.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text asks what specific feature makes a pressure group different from a political party.
hard.simple_explanation: To recognize or point out the difference between two things.
hard.funny_explanation: It's what allows you to tell the difference between your twin cousins, even if they wear the same hat.

examples.text: The way they seek power is what distinguishes a party from a group.
The loud 'Moo' is what distinguishes the cow from the very quiet sheep.

hard.real_world_analogy: A referee blowing a whistle to show the difference between a fair play and a foul.

words.meaning: Public opinions or positions on issues.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to the public opinions or positions that political parties take on certain issues.
hard.simple_explanation: A person's or group's public attitude or position on a specific matter.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like standing with your arms crossed and saying, 'I officially believe cats are better than dogs!'

examples.text: Parties take political stances to win the support of voters.
My stance on ice cream is that it should be eaten at every meal.

hard.real_world_analogy: A goalkeeper standing in the center of the net to show they are ready to block any ball.

words.meaning: To make an effort to do something.
Important subjects people discuss or argue.

medium.simple_explanation: Important topics or problems that people are debating or trying to solve.
medium.funny_explanation: Like the ongoing 'issue' of why the internet always cuts out right when the movie gets good.

examples.text: The two political parties disagreed on many social issues.
I have major issues with anyone who puts pineapple on pizza.

words.meaning: Limited to a small or specific area.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text uses this to say that pressure groups sometimes only involve a small, specific group of people.
hard.simple_explanation: Kept within a certain area or limited to a small number.
hard.funny_explanation: Like when your younger sibling is 'confined' to the playpen so they don't draw on the walls.

examples.text: Some pressure groups are confined to workers of a single factory.
I was confined to my bed because I had the sniffles and the 'lazies'.

hard.real_world_analogy: A bird in a cage compared to a bird flying in the sky.

words.meaning: To include as a necessary part.
Greater in size or amount.
A sum of people or things.
To try to find or get something.
The ability to control people or events.

medium.simple_explanation: The ability or right to control people or things.
medium.funny_explanation: The absolute authority you feel when you're the only one in the house who knows where the TV remote is.

examples.text: Political parties fight to win elections so they can gain power in government.
I wish I had the power to make my homework finish itself while I sleep.

words.meaning: To organize people for a purpose.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It refers to getting people together and ready for action to achieve a political goal.
hard.simple_explanation: To organize and encourage a group of people to take action.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a general shouting 'Avengers Assemble!' to get everyone off the couch and into the fight.

examples.text: Political parties work hard to mobilise voters before an election.
We need to mobilise the neighborhood kids if we want to build the world's biggest snowman.

hard.real_world_analogy: A school fire drill that gets everyone out of the building in an organized way.

words.meaning: To find things that go together.
Long, hard efforts to achieve something.

medium.simple_explanation: Great efforts to overcome difficulties or to achieve something hard.
medium.funny_explanation: The epic daily battle between you and your warm, cozy blanket every single morning.

examples.text: The history books are full of the struggles people faced to win their freedom.
The struggle of trying to look cool while accidentally slipping on a banana peel is real.

words.meaning: To choose from a group.
Right and without any mistakes.
A solution to a question.
Letters or numbers used for identifying.
Provided or stated in a list.
Lower down on a page.
Series of items written one after another.
Relating to one specific thing.

medium.simple_explanation: Referring to one specific person, group, or thing out of many.
medium.funny_explanation: Like that one particular french fry at the bottom of the bag that somehow tastes better than all the others.

examples.text: This group represents the interests of a particular group of farmers.
I am very particular about which socks I wear; they must both be the same level of fuzzy.

words.meaning: Shared by or belonging to many.

medium.simple_explanation: Shared by or belonging to everyone in a group.
medium.funny_explanation: It's common knowledge that if you drop your toast, it will always land butter-side down on the rug.

examples.text: The neighbors worked together for the common good of the community.
Having a messy room is a common trait among people who say 'I'll do it later.'

words.meaning: Started a new activity or plan.

medium.simple_explanation: Started or set a new activity or project in motion.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you 'launch' yourself into the kitchen because you heard a bag of chips opening.

examples.text: The activists launched a huge protest to save the local park.
I launched a mission to find my lost shoe, but I ended up finding three old pens and a sock instead.

words.meaning: A firm decision to solve a problem.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author talks about groups working towards the resolution (solving) of social problems.
hard.simple_explanation: The act of finding an answer or solution to a conflict or problem.
hard.funny_explanation: The glorious moment when you and your friend finally agree on which movie to watch after arguing for an hour.

examples.text: The resolution of the dispute required many meetings.
The resolution to my hunger was a very large peanut butter sandwich.

hard.real_world_analogy: The final click when the last piece of a jigsaw puzzle fits perfectly.

words.meaning: Related to how a group is set up.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe how a group is arranged or managed to function properly.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to how a group or business is set up and structured.
hard.funny_explanation: It's the difference between a messy pile of LEGOs and a shelf where every brick is sorted by color and size.

examples.text: The movement lacked an organisational structure but was still powerful.
My organisational skills are so good that even my socks have their own assigned seats.

hard.real_world_analogy: A school timetable that tells every teacher and student exactly where they need to be.

words.meaning: The way parts of something are arranged.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the 'skeleton' or framework of an organization that keeps it organized.
hard.simple_explanation: The way in which parts of a system are arranged or put together.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of it as the bones inside your body; without structure, you'd just be a blob of human-flavored jelly on the floor.

examples.text: A political party has a very formal structure with leaders and members.
My sandcastle's structure was great until a giant wave decided to sit on it.

hard.real_world_analogy: The wooden frame of a house that holds up the walls and roof.

words.meaning: A way of thinking about something.
To be successful in a competition.
Relating to only one part of society.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This word specifies groups that represent only a particular 'section' or portion of society, like teachers or lawyers.
hard.simple_explanation: Relating to only one part or section of a larger group.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a club that only allows people who like pineapple on pizza—it only cares about that one 'section' of eaters.

examples.text: Sectional interest groups fight for the rights of specific workers.
I have a sectional interest in the toy aisle; I don't care about the boring vegetable section.

hard.real_world_analogy: A single slice of an orange compared to the whole fruit.

words.meaning: Related to all people in a community.
